items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Benefit Street Partners answers questions faster with Codex Anant Kumar builds tools to compare loan valuations and analyze credit agreements, using Codex for code review and faster follow-ups. ~1 day First BDC mark tracker version; ~10–12 total development hours, including refinements. ~20 min First-pass credit agreement analysis, followed by 1+ hour of human review. At Benefit Street Partners, a credit-focused investment manager, answering an investment committee’s follow-up questions used to take days or weeks. Portfolio manager Anant Kumar says analysts can now turn a round of comments in a day with Codex, and often answer questions during the meeting itself. BSP is using these tools to add more review capacity and rigor to underwriting within the same timeframe, rather than to do more deals. “I’ve gone from being just an analyst and a portfolio manager to being a developer as well now. I can build things.” To create a dashboard he could share with colleagues, Kumar used to need someone with software expertise to build a website and pull in the data. Now he builds his own tools, using AI to draft code and review it for errors. His tracker uses public SEC filings from business development companies (BDCs) to compare how firms value the same loan. The team can see how its marks compare with other holders’ valuations. Kumar built the tracker and used Codex for code review. The first version took a day. After adding features and refining the interface over subsequent weeks, he estimates total development time at 10–12 hours total. Kumar’s other tool analyzes credit agreements, which are often 300 pages or longer. Investors need to find clauses that could shift value away from lenders, a task that previously meant asking outside counsel to work through the agreement page by page. Kumar brought together memos from leading law firms on clauses and risks to watch for. He describes the analyzer as a “second brain within our organization.” An uploaded credit agreement takes about 20 minutes to process into a first-pass analysis, followed by an hour or more of human review. BSP has refactored the tool with GPT‑6 Astra, and it is now live in the company-hosted portal. “The AI is very helpful in collating data, ingesting it, synthesizing analysis, but the ultimate investment decision needs to be made by a human,” he says. Underwriting is typically a multi-round process. A round consists of further diligence and a revised memo responding to the investment committee’s questions. Deal timelines range from a few days to a few weeks, so the number of rounds varies. Kumar says, “We feel more confident in our decision making because we have more information at our disposal.” “The quality of my analysis has become so much better and so much faster.” - Built the first BDC tracker in a day, using Codex for code review; about 10–12 hours total including later additions. - Produces a first-pass analysis of a credit agreement in about 20 minutes, followed by an hour or more of human review. - Answers committee follow-up questions faster with Codex, often during the meeting, according to Kumar. BSP is working to connect information across deals. Continuous underwriting is a longer-term aspiration: the team could monitor loans as news happens and examine the effects across its portfolio, rather than re-underwriting only after an event. “Codex has unlocked my day, because I have many more hours in the day to do more high-level work and less routine work,” says Kumar.

items.extracted_excerpt: NVIDIA celebrates the arrival of RTX Spark with retail launch events around the world, bringing gamers, creators and AI enthusiasts together for hands-on experiences.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops are now available, bringing NVIDIA Blackwell RTX graphics, up to 128GB of unified memory and the full NVIDIA AI platform to slim, premium Windows PCs. Starting at $2,399, laptops from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI bring powerful local AI, content creation and gaming capabilities to a portable device, with additional systems on the way. NVIDIA celebrated the launch with events around the world, including one in Berlin, where NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made a surprise appearance. A New Generation of Windows PCs Has Arrived RTX Spark brings decades of NVIDIA accelerated computing innovation into a single superchip, combining an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and NVIDIA Grace CPU with up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and up to 128GB of unified memory. Read more in the press release. RTX Spark Launch Celebrations Light Up Berlin The arrival of RTX Spark brought fans, creators and PC enthusiasts together in Berlin during the Festival of Lights, an annual autumn art festival that transforms the German capital’s most famous landmarks, streets and squares into glowing canvases. This year, the festival featured RTX Spark-themed lighting on the Berlin TV Tower. Fans gathered hours ahead in anticipation for the launch celebration at XPERION, the gaming venue inside Saturn at Alexanderplatz, where attendees got hands-on with RTX Spark laptops from leading PC makers, exploring the latest gaming experiences, content-creation workflows and local AI capabilities. The celebration included a special appearance by Huang, who greeted an enthusiastic crowd, passed out popcorn and posed for selfies. He also gave out five personally signed RTX Spark laptops. Berlin held one of six RTX Spark retail launch celebrations worldwide. From San Francisco to Seoul: How the World Welcomed RTX Spark A massive crowd gathered at the JD MALL Shuangjing Store in Beijing to celebrate the highly anticipated launch, enjoying a night of innovation and community connection. Attendees at Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı in Istanbul experienced a lively event filled with interactive demonstrations and specialized programming led by local creators. Seoul’s COEX East Lobby transformed into a bustling hub of creativity, hosting an eager crowd for engaging hands-on demos and captivating evening sessions dedicated to gaming and AI. Tech enthusiasts in San Francisco visited the local Best Buy store for an unforgettable morning of hands-on RTX Spark demos, fireside chats with local founders and a special appearance by tech influencer iJustine. The energy at Muse Garden in Taipei was electric as the local AI community came together for a vibrant evening of music, engaging discussions and incredible product showcases. Developers and AI enthusiasts can explore NVIDIA-tested recipes, playbooks and resources for running local AI on RTX Spark. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X. See notice regarding software product information.

items.extracted_title: AI Gateway logs now show session affinity - Vercel
items.extracted_excerpt: Vercel AI Gateway logs now group requests into sessions, with cache hit rate, cost, turns, and the coding agent behind each conversation.
items.extracted_text_for_analysis: AI Gateway logs now have a Sessions view that groups requests into sessions and shows how session affinity routed each one. Each row shows the coding agent or app that ran the session, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, along with its cost, models, providers, and how much of its input was cached across every turn. Open a session to see its cache hit rate, duration, and path. The path lists each turn with its model and timing, and names the provider serving the session along with any earlier ones. Session affinity sends each turn to the provider that served the one before it, so the provider already has most of the prompt in cache. A session that stays on one provider reads more of each prompt from cache. Filter sessions by turns, client, model, provider, authentication, or cost. Single-turn sessions are hidden until you clear the minimum turns filter. Session affinity runs by default on text and chat requests. To group requests yourself, send the same sessionId in providerOptions.gateway, or the same x-session-id header, on every request in a conversation. Requests without one are grouped by a fingerprint of the conversation's opening and appear as fingerprinted sessions. Read the session affinity documentation for more information on how AI Gateway identifies sessions.

items.extracted_text_for_analysis: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is now available on AI Gateway. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash that improves reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and image understanding. The coding gains show up in terminal work and in building and editing whole repositories, and the agentic gains in multi-step automation. With images, the model reads charts and handles visual reasoning more accurately when it can call tools. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 also finishes tasks faster and with shorter outputs than the previous snapshot, so agent runs tend to take less time and use fewer output tokens. Use deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 as the model name: import { streamText } from 'ai'; const result = streamText({ model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017', prompt: 'Write a script that retries failed uploads with exponential backoff.',}); To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: npx vercel ai-gateway setup Try DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 in the model playground. AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.

items.extracted_text_for_analysis: Glimpse from Elorian is now available on AI Gateway. The visual reasoning model accepts images and video to follow objects through motion, interpret spatial relationships, and connect an action to its physical consequences. Glimpse can return to visual evidence as it works: zooming into a detail, revisiting a short interval of video, or tracking the same feature across frames. This allows the model to support use cases like scientific chart analysis, video captioning, visual counting, and robotics data annotation. Some examples include checking a train's motion to determine whether it is slowing down, keeping objects distinct through camera movement, and labeling completed actions in robot footage. Use elorian/glimpse as the model name: import { streamText } from 'ai'; const result = streamText({ model: 'elorian/glimpse', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: [ { type: 'text', text: 'Describe this image in one sentence.' }, { type: 'file', mediaType: 'image/jpeg', data: new URL('https://elorian.ai/assets/blog/glimpse/open-pliers.jpg'), }, ], }], maxOutputTokens: 4096, reasoning: 'low'}); for await (const text of result.textStream) { process.stdout.write(text);} With AI SDK 7, you can send a video as a file part. Replace the placeholder URL with a public or signed HTTPS URL for your video: import { streamText } from 'ai'; const result = streamText({ model: 'elorian/glimpse', maxOutputTokens: 4096, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: [ { type: 'text', text: 'Describe the visible scene in at most five words.
